blocking_issues.issue: The Q2 2026 comparative GDP chart labels the EU year-on-year growth rate 1.2% and France 0.7%, whereas Eurostat's 7 September 2026 harmonised Q2 release reports EU 1.4% and France 0.5%. The 1.2% value is the euro-area rate, not the EU rate. The draft uses Polish GUS 3.9% alongside Eurostat-style peer comparisons without disclosing the harmonisation difference (Eurostat's seasonally adjusted Poland figure is 3.8%). The same errors appear in both locales.

The 3.9% GUS value may be retained as a separately defined national estimate, but should not be silently mixed into a harmonised cross-country comparison.

This materially confuses an older financing envelope with the current approved plan.
